questions.note: Head height (~220 px against the reference's ~235 in the full pair), shoulder span and arm drop match within a few percent; long legs are declared. Torso and limbs read lean and young because the garments add no thickness, so the man looks narrower through the deltoids and hips than the reference's bulked-up soldier.

Stance, foot spacing and both elbow positions overlay well in the onion. The figure stands more upright and the chin is lifted, losing the reference's slight back-lean; the carbine line is steeper and higher (partly the declared real-size gun). Shoulder outline is smaller because the pauldrons are thin cards instead of domed shells.

Every item is present and roughly where drawn, radio antenna on the left back included. Against that: a rear belt pouch hangs off the hip, a thin elbow disc sits off the left elbow, the belt is a narrow strap rather than a padded battle belt, and the boots read as sneakers.

Order is right but layers have no thickness: trousers and shirt are painted on the body (crotch, seat, shoulder blades show through). Carrier shoulder flaps and the right pauldron stand off as flat planes with gaps; the left elbow disc and the rear hip pouch float. The carbine clears arms and carrier.

The reference man is bulked by loose combat shirt, padded sleeves, layered plates and baggy G3-style trousers. The render is a slim body in skin-tight cloth with flat plates; thighs and seat read as leggings, upper arms as smooth tubes. Below the knee the trouser balloons into a stiff tube, so mass is wrong in both directions.

Right hand sits under the receiver with the index finger laid along it, a real trigger-discipline grip; stock tucks inside the right forearm, gun carried well forward of the thighs. Left hand clamps the handguard from above with fingers hanging and the palm not seated on it; the wrist bend is sharp. Reads as a posed hold, not a weight-bearing one.

defects.what: Trousers are skin-tight through hips, crotch, thighs and seat: the crotch bulge and buttock forms show through, then the leg flares into a stiff baggy tube below the knee.
defects.fix: Crye G3-class trousers hang with 40-60 mm ease at the thigh, a gusseted crotch and a straight seat; volume is continuous from hip to cuff.

defects.what: Combat shirt body and sleeves are painted onto the skin: no fabric ease at shoulders, elbows or upper arms; arms read as smooth tubes and the shoulder blades show in the back view.
defects.fix: A combat shirt's sleeves carry padding and 20-30 mm ease, with fold mass at the elbow crook and armpit.

defects.what: The right pauldron is a flat thin card tilted off the shoulder, its top edge standing clear of the deltoid instead of a domed shell following it.
defects.fix: A shoulder guard is a moulded shell of 3-5 mm wall that cups the deltoid and is strapped down to it.

defects.what: Carrier shoulder strap panels kink upward as flat planes and stand off the trapezius with a visible gap, on both shoulders.
defects.fix: JPC-class shoulder straps are padded webbing lying on the trapezius under tension from the plate weight.

defects.what: Pauldron, arm bands and forearm guard render as dark grey painted metal with bright white paint chips; the reference armour is tan-olive polymer with worn edges.
defects.fix: Polymer armour scuffs to a paler matte of its own colour along edges, not bright metal under paint; base value should be mid tan-grey.

defects.what: Knee pads are rounded pillow boxes in black with tan blotches, value inverted from the reference's tan hard caps in a dark frame, with no cap-and-sleeve construction.
defects.fix: AirFlex-class pads: a contoured hard cap over a thinner foam body, cap edges framed, strap slots at the sides.

defects.what: A rear belt pouch hangs well behind the hip with its flap jutting outward, not seated against the belt or the body.
defects.fix: A belt-mounted pouch rides flush on the belt's MOLLE, its back against the belt with no gap.

defects.what: A thin disc stands edge-on off the outer left elbow, floating clear of the sleeve, instead of an elbow pad wrapping the joint.
defects.fix: An elbow pad is a curved cap of 15-25 mm foam with a hard shell, strapped around the joint.

defects.what: The right boot reads as a sneaker bootie: one smooth wrapped upper, no toe cap or rand, a thin wedge sole, and laces only on the ankle shaft.
defects.fix: Zephyr-class boots lace from the toe box to the collar, with suede and textile panels, a rubber toe rand and a 30-40 mm lugged sole.

defects.what: Hair is a solid cap with a hard edge across the forehead and temples and spiky polygon tufts on the crown; it reads as a helmet or a painted skull.
defects.fix: Short hair thins at the hairline into skin and stands as fine strands, darker at the roots.

defects.what: Left hand clamps the handguard from above with the thumb over the rail and fingers hanging, the palm not seated against the handguard.
defects.fix: A support hand cups the handguard from beneath or wraps it, palm in contact, fingers closed around it.

defects.what: Gloves are smooth rubber with thick sausage fingers and no knuckle or finger protection.
defects.fix: M-Pact-class gloves have TPR knuckle and finger guards, a seamed back and a palm patch.

ranked: [D1] The trousers are tights: crotch and seat sculpted through the cloth, thighs skin-tight, then a stiff baggy tube below the knee. Real G3-style trousers have even ease and a gusseted crotch.
[D2] The shirt and sleeves are painted on: no ease anywhere, upper arms are smooth cylinders and the back view shows shoulder blades. The reference's bulk comes from padded sleeves.
Overall mass is far below the reference: a lean young body in skin-tight cloth with thin flat plates, against a man bulked by layered kit. Even with correct placement it reads as a costume.
[D5] Armour material reads as painted steel: dark grey with bright white chips. The reference's plates are tan-olive polymer that wears paler at the edges.
[D3] The right pauldron is a flat card tilted off the shoulder; real shoulder guards are moulded shells that cup the deltoid. The pauldrons also make the shoulder outline smaller than drawn.
[D4] Carrier shoulder straps kink up off the trapezius as flat planes with daylight under them; under a plate's weight real straps lie flat and bear on the shoulder.
[D6] Knee pads are pillow boxes with inverted values (black with tan blotches). The reference shows tan hard caps in dark frames.
[D9] Boots read as sneakers: smooth wrapped uppers, thin wedge soles, no toe cap, laces only at the ankle. A Zephyr-class boot laces from the toe box and has a deep lugged sole.
[D10] Hair is a hard-edged cap with spiky tufts on the crown; it gives the head away at native size even with the declared default skin.
Trouser lower legs are much lighter (pale grey) than the reference's charcoal with tan dirt; the leg value jumps from dark at the thigh to near-white at the cuff.
[D7] A rear belt pouch hangs off the back of the hip with its flap jutting out; it is not carried by the belt.
[D8] A thin disc floats edge-on off the left elbow where the reference has an elbow pad.
The battle belt is a narrow flat strap; a belt carrying thigh rigs and pouches is about 50 mm wide and padded, and should read as a band at the waist.
Posture is more upright than the reference, with the chin lifted, so the man looks up and out rather than settled back on his heels.
[D11] The left hand clamps the handguard from above with fingers dangling; it does not look as though it is bearing the carbine's weight.
Carrier colour is a desaturated khaki-grey with a flat plate face and no webbing rows; the reference's carrier is olive-coyote with PALS and visible pouch bulk.
[D12] Gloves are smooth rubber with thick, rounded fingers and no knuckle guards.
Trouser cuffs stop short above the boot collar instead of breaking over the boot tops as the reference shows.
